scope: Background production for all current authored nodes. This plan does not assert that images exist or have passed visual review.
generationGate: No paid submissions until the reported OpenQI credit blocker is resolved.
commonRules: Original late-1990s Japanese animation background painting, controlled architectural drawing, opaque gouache and watercolor material texture on backgrounds only.
Request 16:9 4K, inspect actual returned dimensions, retain original pixels and never upscale to satisfy a dimension claim.
Readable medium values and clear depth. Reserve the lower dialogue region and right-center character placement without blanking most of the scene.
Separate people from background layers. No baked faces, silhouettes, portrait photographs or unidentified extra cast. Phones and remote calls do not place the other person physically in this room.
No baked lettering, game UI, logos, collages or readable maps. Precise clues and records belong in the game's accessible text, not generated pseudo-writing.

Red is reserved for a focal practical signal or small material accent; cool gray, paper white, oxidized metal and restrained amber maintain material separation. No full-frame brown darkness, neon haze or glossy CGI.
Use an accepted base image as a real reference for dependent variants, preserving doors, windows, routes and furniture. Dependencies must be reviewed before their variants are submitted.
Endings may span several locations. Their listed background represents one specific authored moment, never an invented montage or a claim about the original novel ending.

jobs.brief: Existing training-room background and two reviewed Fang Nuo expressions. Preserve this room as the material and daylight anchor; no regeneration required.

Old commercial-building tiled washroom at 10:03, mirror, sinks and a visible stall-door edge. Restrained cool daylight, sink reflection without a body or face. Clear unoccupied space carries the aftermath of the overheard conversation.

Open-plan office at 14:20, boxy computers, files, ordinary dark desks and tall iron-mullion windows in the same renovated building. Visible blank monitor, keyboard and paper corner; readable workplace, not another classroom.

Small office kitchenette after work: kettle, two water cups, narrow window, a cleared table for notes. Dusk paper-white sky and modest warm interior light. The witness ending uses its opening shared-records moment here.

18:15 commercial-building entrance with glass revolving door. Old shopping street branches right; staffed metro stair entrance is visibly left. Ordinary broad pavement in the established old iron-and-stone city. Keep route geometry readable without signs or people.

18:42 corner convenience store interior: street-facing counter, cup and small oden tray, grocery shelves, warm practical ceiling lights. Through the window on image-right, a short alley visibly ends at a stone wall. No fantasy tavern or cafe substitution.

Street-side view of the same short alley around 18:42-19:06. Convenience-store glazing anchors left foreground; hooks remain in the end wall. Window reflection and real street stay spatially coherent. No glowing portal or baked street-name puzzle; the text carries the one-character discrepancy.

18:39 metro concourse, ticket barriers, empty glass service counter and ordinary timetable panels inside older iron-and-stone construction. Public, functional and visibly connected to the entrance. A platform or grand railway hall would be the wrong location.

Fang Nuo's modest tidy home at night: desk lamp from left, computer, plain notes, water cup, a small storage box, visible locked door and city window. The blend ending is represented by rediscovering the folded note beside that box. No bedroom glamour or baked readable correspondence.

Same shop, counter, window and alley at 11:00 next day. Relight to overcast daylight; a plain full paper cup replaces the meal tray. Preserve layout so the observer's explanation concerns the same place.

Beyond the crossed threshold, familiar street steps and a distant bus-stop pole under dusk lamps. Preserve real street structure but shift viewpoint to the newly reached side. No station woman, no glowing doorway, no claim of a solved written sign in the bitmap.

22:14 worn apartment landing: shallow stair run, close neighboring doors and scuffed handrail. Newly replaced practical light, one restrained emergency-red accent. The player's door and adjacent neighbor door must both be legible. Danger is conveyed by the confined layout, not a painted attacker.

Li Yu's cramped living room behind the adjoining door: simple table with exactly two cream-cake portions and unwrapped forks, close wall and visible locked exit. A bookcase hides the later photo wall. Familiar domestic shapes with uneasy controlled night light, no affectionate couple composition.

Window-side angle in the same room. Window opens only a hand's width; broken concrete equipment ledge lies outside at a clearly dangerous height. Small camera support by curtain points toward the opposite building. The bookcase is reflected in glass; no body or private photograph is baked in.

Close view beside the washroom: running tap, old tile, frosted glass door and narrow gap to the living room. Telephone caller remains offsite. Use a hard practical lamp and deeper door recess while retaining enough detail to read the player's limited space.

Bookcase now pulled away to expose a wall of small photograph backs and indistinct framed shapes. Do not bake identifiable faces, nudity or extra character designs into photos; discovery details stay in narrative text. Tied rubbish bag and delivery-paper shapes under the table connect the evidence.

Angle from kitchen/living-room threshold toward the open apartment door and blocked stairwell line beyond. Scraped worktop and door latch are visible. No floating weapon, fight figures or graphic marks; those actions belong to separately reviewed scene layers or text.

Inner end of the same corridor with the older resident's closed door, small threshold and utility recess nearby. The collective ending represents the later tool-return visit at this same closed door. Never show the elder in the corridor during the locked-door conversation.

Water-meter recess, half bundle of old newspapers and faded fire-plan board. The old platform is to the right and visibly sealed; left leads toward apartment doors. Draw blank diagram shapes only: exact map directions are supplied by accessible scene text.

Interior behind a heavy closed apartment door at 22:35-22:38. Low-angle view includes latch, lowered handle and a strip of ordinary floor for the exhausted player. No police operator inside the room; their voice comes through the phone.

Outside the same apartment at 22:51: entrance steps, newly replaced lamp, curb and partial service-vehicle light reflected on masonry. Red practical reflection is restrained; no siren glow filter over the full painting. Keep the wall by the steps reachable in composition.

Temporary reception desk under clear neutral fluorescent light. Charging lead, cup, paper forms and a simple chair on each side. No prison bars or interrogation spectacle. Phone screen and forms have no readable generated text.

New rental room after the move: boxes, half-open curtain toward an empty lot, window-side lamp and a document envelope on the desk. Layout must differ visibly from Li Yu's room. Quiet evening clarity, no surveillance camera introduced into the empty view.

Morning at a family guest room. Closed bathroom door, bed edge and hot breakfast bowl set outside the room's partly opened entrance. A calm lived-in place separate from both old apartments; no injury close-up, no unexpected guest.

Modest rental kitchen/dining corner at 20:40. Worn small table, two bowls of noodles, halved soft egg, chopsticks and crumpled cash. Compact domestic proportions contrast later wealth. No folded-receipt prop from the rejected old concept; no baked people.

Exclusive club corridor at 21:12, mirrored wall and partly open private-room door with tray clearance. Wine glasses and fruit plate visible through the doorway, restrained red upholstery and old silver fittings. Expensive through craftsmanship, not neon casino lighting.

Outside the same club at 21:20 beside an understated parked car. Visible door handle and curb, practical entrance lamps reflected on glass. Preserve facade materials from the club interior; no sports-car advertisement or model pose.

Same rental at 22:02-22:30, view includes entrance and table. Noodle dishes cleared, small unopened cake box with plain seasonal ribbon and paper cups on the table; kettle behind. Preserve the room's exact doors and furniture. No luxury tableware suddenly added.

Same rental kitchen/window at morning. Milk bottle with overlapping blank labels, bread bag and clipped opening near sink. Cool daylight and modest warm materials. The equal ending uses the established shared home; later unaltered milk packaging may need a small prop variant after review.

Same late-night table after the cake has been moved aside. Blank papers, pen, two keys and cups form the practical center; enough empty paper is visible for the agreement. Do not invent readable income numbers, signatures or extra belongings.

Du Mansheng's own spacious home at 07:50, much larger than the rental: tall plain windows, generous distance between furniture, single cup and bread beside an opened planner. Restrained quality materials and unoccupied space convey her change of circumstances.

Du family reception/dining room at 16:20, formal table with one pulled-out chair and blank gold-edged place cards. Polished older craftsmanship and tall windows without excessive gold decor. The empty assigned seat matters more than an imposing mansion panorama.

Same family's private study at 17:00: tea cup with separate lid, broad desk, family-photo frame turned at a non-readable angle, sofa and closed door behind the player's viewpoint. Detailed room boundaries, no extra family faces painted into the background.

Family home doorway at 18:10. Outside step, open door, garden wall and curb where either pickup car could arrive. Show no arriving car yet: the player has not entered either. Same exterior masonry and window proportions as the family's interior sets.

Small street restaurant around 19:30, simple wobbling table with folded paper under one leg, two noodle bowls, chopsticks and tea pot/cups. Soft practical lantern fixtures with crisp painted structure; the restart ending uses a later conversation at this established modest meeting place.

First night after moving: a new independent home with partially unpacked boxes, takeaway noodles with one egg, cup and phone by the table. A second set of chopsticks marks the friend's visit without baking a person into the image. Distinct from rental and expansive former home.

Physical-feeling ability selection chamber with a shelving wall; one small warm gold coin remains on the lowest shelf while other compartments are dark. Late-1990s sci-fi architecture and clean perspective. No readable menus, holographic gradients or crowds; rules and 99/100/101 are text-layer facts.

Temporary wind-battered shelter on the Pacific island, 36th preparation day. Mountain ridges frame central buildable flat ground, open sea beyond. Table with blank site plan, two equipment sheets held by a water cup, ordinary survey kit. Plausible civil works, no fortress or tactical base.

Underground supply facility during preparation: modular compartments recede beyond the main aisle, ventilation ducts, sealed food/water/medical crates and an idle forklift with two sheets on its hood. Clean new painted surfaces, neutral lights and a single red locator. Storage capacity shown through space, not piles of decorative cargo.

Construction completion office one week before disaster: desk, coffee-stained blank roster, acceptance binder, work helmets on hooks and open view toward the departure ferry landing. No staff faces in the background; the imminent departure is grounded by ferry equipment and packed personal bags.

Functional island observation/logistics room after local rain stops: salt-streaked window toward sea, boxy communications monitors, physical storage-chart board, nearby blank packing sheets and a warm bowl beside keyboard. Clear cloudy daylight. Other speakers remain on remote channels; screens show non-legible signal shapes, not invented people or written figures.

06:40 equipment observation corridor with running baseline water-treatment plant visible through glass, separate reserve cabinet with plain inspection seal, storage tank and tool cabinet. Readable maintenance access; no total blackout, flooded island machinery or explosion, because the baseline plant still works.

Same observation/communications room at night. Warm task lamp from left, cool sea window and dim limited green device status; screens have restrained unlettered panes. Preserve working light on desk and routes. No meeting participants physically around the table: these are voice/video channels.

Same observation room before sunrise. Two active plain monitor panes and visible recording equipment, salt-marked window, gold coin beside keyboard. Cool dawn horizon, modest task light; exact names, timestamps and records remain readable game text rather than generated graphics.

Night project archive room: practical shelf files, acceptance binders and desk with three blank monitor windows. A group-photo sheet is present only as indistinct print shapes without identifiable faces. Endings show record collation here, not proof of the missing workers' presence or survival.

07:20 covered island dock, white salt line on retaining wall, narrow service walkway, modest transport vessel, sealed maintenance tools and checklist clipboard. Clear waterline and unobstructed boarding route. Boat belongs to a finite transport operation, not a colossal warship or luxury yacht.

Island-side communication desk at 16:15 while the vessel is at a remote receiving point. Shared room geometry, speaker, physical loading chart and screen with simplified hull/waterline imagery. Do not move the player onto the boat or put remote mainland staff on the island. Precise loading tradeoff stays in choice text.

Storage vault threshold with one row of lights, thick ordinary sealed door, key cylinder, marked personal inventory sheets and visible communication indicator in adjoining room. Preserve depot architecture; security is functional winter shelter infrastructure, not stacked armor or magical vault ornament.

Same dock after the rainy season in morning light, wet adult-sized travel bags drying on landing and an ordinary allocation/work-schedule board near warehouse. People remain separate scene layers. Show active habitation through practical objects without inventing unlimited capacity or victory banners.

Night communication watch in the same room: real paper sea chart, penciled unlettered route segments, arrival log and distant small fixed harbor signal beyond window. Represent the narrator's actual watch at the radio; no fantasy fleet or triumphant arrival montage.

Same quiet observation room arranged for one-person dinner: single bowl and chopsticks, weekly maintenance sheet under the gold coin, ordinary working climate control and faint inactive channel panes. Material comfort remains intact; avoid visual claims of death, hunger or a completed system victory.
